title: Reopening Strait of Hormuz Would Ease Oil Crisis but Only So Much
partialText: Analysts said energy and shipping companies would be reluctant to fully restore operations until they were confident that hostilities were over.

title: With Vaccines Widely Popular, Kennedy Changes Tone, but Maybe Not His Plans
partialText: Several moves suggest Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. could revive his campaign to question the safety and effectiveness of the shots after the midterm elections.

title: Trump Will Participate in a Marathon Bible Reading
partialText: He will read a passage from the Old Testament that his Christian supporters cite as a call to national repentance and divine blessing.

title: Trump Signs Executive Order to Loosen Restrictions on Psychedelic Drugs
partialText: The president’s executive order is intended to accelerate research into the compounds’ efficacy in treating mental health disorders like severe depression and PTSD.

title: White House and Anthropic Hold ‘Productive’ Meeting, Aiming for a Compromise
partialText: Friday’s meeting at the White House followed the introduction of Anthropic’s powerful new artificial intelligence model, Mythos, which U.S. officials believe could be critical for security.

title: The Doctor Will Seek Your Vote Now
partialText: Dozens of Democratic doctors are running for office in the midterms, including some spurred by opposition to Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his anti-vaccine stance.

title: ‘Turning Point Was Charlie Kirk’: Why This Student Group Moved On
partialText: Students at the University of Arkansas disagreed with Turning Point’s direction, pointing to challenges ahead for the conservative group.

title: Primary Becomes Purity Test for a State G.O.P.: ‘You Can’t Serve Two Masters’
partialText: For years, Republican state legislators in Montana have been willing to team up with Democrats, but in nearly two dozen races on June 2, a nationally attuned right has those lawmakers in its sights.

title: Maduro’s Successor Is Purging Allies Who Kept Him in Power in Venezuela
partialText: The successor to Venezuela’s captured President Nicolás Maduro is purging the people who kept him in power.

title: Pope Says News Outlets Misread Some of His Remarks as Criticism of Trump
partialText: Pope Leo responded directly on Monday to a presidential attack. But since then, he said, some of his statements during his Africa trip have been misconstrued.

title: In Angola, Pope Leo XIV Faces the Legacy of Colonialism
partialText: His visit includes a trip to a shrine where enslaved Africans were baptized before being forced into the treacherous voyage across the Atlantic Ocean.

title: The Pope Bedevils Trump
partialText: A higher authority finally tells Trump he’s no messiah.

title: Trump Still Hearts McKinley
partialText: Trump loves the 19th century. But why?

title: Trading Spaces
partialText: With spring comes the urge to spring-clean. It’s about so much more than just organizing your closet.

title: After D4vd Arrest, Lake Elsinore Residents Mourn Celeste Rivas Hernandez
partialText: Celeste Rivas Hernandez went missing from Lake Elsinore, Calif., at age 13. The musician known as D4vd has been detained in connection with her death.

title: Who Is the New Leader of Hungary?
partialText: Our reporter Andrew Higgins describes why Hungary’s voters chose Peter Magyar over Viktor Orban in a landslide, ending Orban’s 16 years in power.

title: New PEPFAR Data Show Worrying Declines in Testing and Treatment for H.I.V.
partialText: The numbers are the first to quantify the effect of the Trump administration’s shutdown and restarting of a program that has saved millions of lives worldwide.

title: Migrant Children Removed From New York Shelter After Abuse Allegations
partialText: Federal officials received complaints about the treatment of children and adolescents at a facility in Westchester County, N.Y.

title: Tornados Reported Across the Midwest as Powerful Storms Slam the Region
partialText: One reported tornado downed trees and damaged cars in Lena, Ill., an official said.
